 Source: Reach Media / Radio One Bassam Tariq on The Morning Hustle: Blade, Mahershala Ali and Hustle
 Filmmaker Bassam Tariq stopped by The Morning Hustle and called Atlanta his “third home,” after Houston and New York. Atlanta is where his family was based while he worked on Blade . Houston is where his working-class family moved for affordable living and where he went to middle and high school.
 ✕ 
 Marvel handed him a huge budget for the highly anticipated Blade . The project fell apart, but Tariq has no regrets. The job paid off his parents’ mortgage and taught him to honor an audience’s time. He also defended artists who take commercial gigs: “You gotta eat.”
 Tariq wrote his new film for Mahershala Ali but was too intimidated to send the script. Friends Bradford Young and Ramy Youssef pushed him to do it, and Ali signed on right away. He wants fans in theaters and compared a packed screening to church. He also said streaming has real value because it gives more people access to films.
 Your Mother, Your Mother, Your Mother traces back to 2014. That year, his wife was hospitalized after childbirth and his newborn son went two days without milk. The title comes from a prophetic saying that gives mothers three times the honor owed to fathers.
 His advice for young creators is “story, story, story.” He recommends making five-minute shorts instead of flashy camera reels, finding your voice, building grit and leaning on your community.
